thread:
maria: Heads-up — CI SBOM job quarantined the `templates` artifact. Rule: METADATA_DRIFT. hashes match but metadata.version and author fields differ from lockfile. link: https://ci.internal/reports/1718243340
sec-bot: Automated alert: SBOM provenance mismatch for `templates:sha256:8f3a...` (severity=medium). Triggered quarantine and registry block.
jason: Can someone paste the minimal diff? Is this a benign normalization or potential tamper?
maria: Minimal diff: `package.json` metadata.author changed from "vendor-inc" -> "vendor-inc <ci@builder>" and `homepage` removed. No code-layer diffs.
olivia: Which builder image produced the artifact? New builder image rolled on 2024-06-11. CI job ran on builders/ubuntu-2204-2024-06-11.
samir: I see the same commit rebuilt at 2024-06-11T04:12Z by token `ci-deploy-bot.ctl`. SBOM fields differ only in non-functional metadata.
maria: Repro locally with pinned sources + older builder -> SBOM matches original. So looks like builder metadata normalization. Still policy flags it.
jason: OK containment checklist: 1) revoke builder token 2) block pushes to `templates` 3) create incident and assign 4) run verified rebuild on locked builder image 5) review SBOM policy.
maria: Requested token revoke from IAM: request id `iam-req-20240612-01`.
sec-bot: iam.revoke_token(ci-deploy-bot.ctl) — success (by automation)
devops-bot: registry.protect_tag(`templates`) — push blocked for non-admin tokens.
olivia: KMS question: were artifacts signed with `redwood-prod-sign-v1`? SBOM shows no signature field on this artifact. KMS audit lookup in progress.
samir: KMS logs: sign operation for `templates:sha256:8f3a...` at 2024-06-11T04:12Z by `ci-deploy-bot.ctl` using key `redwood-prod-sign-v1`. Signature existed but signature verification failed during ingest due to metadata mismatch in SBOM consumer.
maria: Action items proposed: (A) Verified rebuild using pinned builder + re-sign with current KMS key, (B) Add normalization rules to SBOM comparator to ignore benign metadata fields (author formatting/homepage), (C) Add explicit runbook step for METADATA_DRIFT including who can approve overrides.
jason: RBAC gap: who can approve a quarantine override today? Answer: only `sec-admins`. Suggest creating `release-manager` role with `quarantine:approve` scoped to repos they own; requires 2FA and justification.
olivia: Agree, but require that any approval writes an audit entry: approver, timestamp, justification, diff link. Retention 1 year minimum.
sec-bot: Incident ticket created: `INC-20240612-templates-sbom-drift` (severity: P2).
maria: Assigning owners: samir (rebuild + validation), olivia (KMS + audit), jason (RBAC + policy updates).
samir: Starting verified rebuild on `ubuntu-2204-locked-2024-05` now. Will publish new SBOM + attach signature once complete.
maria: For immediate mitigation: please add an alert rule to detect frequent METADATA_DRIFT spikes (>3 in 24h) and page sec-oncall.
jason: I'll open a PR to add `release-manager` role and the approval audit hook. Pinging people for review.
olivia: We'll also schedule KMS key rotation advisory for `redwood-prod-sign-v1` — no evidence of compromise but rotate on next maintenance window.
maria: Post-incident follow-ups we need documented: (1) SBOM comparator ruleset update, (2) RBAC change + audit retention policy, (3) CI builder base version pinning guidance, (4) monitoring rule for drift spikes.
samir: Rebuild finished: new artifact `templates:sha256:ab12...` SBOM attached and signature verified. Pushing for controlled redeploy.
maria: Thanks. I'll close the incident when RBAC PR merged and SBOM comparator patch is deployed.
jason: +1. Also add a short blameless note in the weekly security roundup about this false-positive class so product teams know what to expect. :memo:
sec-bot: Incident INC-20240612 closed (resolved) by `maria` at 2024-06-12T09:11:00Z
